ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An electronic transformer is one of the key pieces of equipment in a digital substation. As shown in the figure, the principle of the probe of a certain electronic voltage transformer is resistance voltage division; the resistance between ac is (n-1) times the resistance between cd. In a certain measurement, the reading of the digital voltmeter at the output end is U, then what is the voltage at the input end?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the upper part is marked with the input end, and the two input contacts are respectively a on the left side and b on the right side; the lower part is marked with the output end, and the two output contacts are respectively c and d. The right side from b to d is the same vertical wire, therefore b and d belong to the same potential end; c is a voltage-division tap led out from the middle position. The gray resistor body in the figure represents a resistance voltage-division structure from a through c to d, and the output voltmeter measures the voltage between c and d. Then reason: The problem statement gives that the resistance between ac is (n-1) times the resistance between cd. Let R_cd=R, then R_ac=(n-1)R. The voltage between the input ends a and b is equivalent to the voltage between a and d, corresponding to the total series resistance R_ac+R_cd=(n-1)R+R=nR. The reading of the digital voltmeter at the output end is U, that is, U_cd=U. In series voltage division, voltage is directly proportional to resistance, so U_ab/U_cd=(nR)/R=n, therefore U_ab=nU.
